records.name: Brewerytown Sharswood Community Civic Association
records.summary: Neighbors in Brewerytown and Sharswood who review zoning requests for nearby building projects. Each month they hold a Zoom meeting where residents hear from applicants and vote, then they send the Zoning Board of Adjustment their position.
records.what_you_do: The zoning committee reviews building projects between 19th and 33rd streets, from Cecil B. Moore Avenue south to Girard Avenue, hears from applicants, and sends the Zoning Board of Adjustment its position. Residents who register can comment and vote on each request.

schedule.text: Public community zoning meetings are on Zoom on the third Thursday of each month, 6:30 to 8:30 pm. The zoning subcommittee meets the first Tuesday of each month.

first_step.how: Register in advance for the next Zoom community zoning meeting, using the web form, email, or phone number on the zoning page, then join on the third Thursday evening.
first_step.basis: The zoning page says any neighbor can register to attend and comment, with three ways to sign up, but it does not say newcomers are specially welcomed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The community meeting runs on Zoom from 6:30 to 8:30 pm. Applicants present a project, and registered neighbors can ask questions or comment for up to two minutes each. Each registered person gets one vote per project, and any vote made after the session ends does not count.
first_visit_tips: Register ahead using the web form, email, or phone number on the zoning page.
Have your name, phone number, and address ready, since the sign-up asks for them.
Keep comments short, because each one is limited to two minutes.
If you join by phone, you will get voting instructions during the meeting.

records.notes: Zoom schedule, registration methods and voting rules come from the zoning page. The calendar and news items carry no years, so the 2026 sign of life rests on the 2026 registration link on the zoning page. The month is carried from tier 1 and is not confirmed. The subcommittee's membership is not described. The home page lists two other group email addresses (outreach and office) that were not added. No dues or fees are listed, so cost was left out.

records.name: Community Schools @Edward Gideon School
records.summary: A Community School partnership between the City, the School District and neighbors, Edward Gideon School welcomes volunteers through the City's volunteer portal.
records.what_you_do: Help with the school's weekly food handouts for neighbors, walk students to school safely, and support family events such as game nights.

first_step.how: Email the school's community program contact to ask which volunteer roles are open, then start the clearance paperwork.
first_step.basis: Volunteers must finish background clearances before starting, so the first step is paperwork rather than an open door.
first_step.what_to_expect: Before a first shift you will need several checks: state child abuse history and criminal background clearances, an FBI waiver or fingerprinting, a school district code of conduct and certificate, and a city release form. Some roles also ask for an orientation. The volunteer listing does not give a shift length or a cost.
first_visit_tips: Start the clearance paperwork early, since the listing requires it before volunteering.
Ask the school contact which roles need an orientation and when the first shift can start.

records.notes: The volunteer listing returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool during this pass and was not retried. Tasks, clearances and contacts come from the tier 1 read on 2026-10-08. No shift times or cost appear in any readable source. The listing mentions the Philly Reading Coaches program, covered in the Paul L. Dunbar record and in leads_only.

records.name: Community Schools @Paul L. Dunbar
records.summary: A Community School partnership between the City, the School District and neighbors, Paul L. Dunbar welcomes volunteers through the City's volunteer portal.
records.what_you_do: Read one on one with an elementary student through the Philly Reading Coaches program. The volunteer listing said reading coaches were the only role being recruited at the school when it was read on 2026-10-08.

first_step.how: Email the school's community program contact to ask about current reading coach openings and the next training date.
first_step.basis: Reading coaches make a weekly commitment, and neither the volunteer listing nor the city page we could read gives a start date or training steps, so the way in is not clear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Reading coaches sit one on one with a student in grades K to 3 for at least an hour a week, after school. The city's November 2023 program page says no experience is needed and volunteers must be 16 or older, though the current cycle may differ. Ask the school contact for the current checks, training, and session times before you commit.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the current checks and training with the school contact before you sign up.
Plan for a regular weekly hour, since the role asks for steady attendance.
Ask which days and hours your session would be before you commit.

records.notes: The volunteer listing returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool during this pass and was not retried, so the reading coach opening and contact come from the tier 1 read on 2026-10-08. The only program detail readable is a November 2023 city article, which may be out of date. A search snippet from a lead-only job board, not opened, suggested the spring 2026 cycle had ended. Confirm current openings before promoting. The site had no more detail than tier 1.

records.name: PSPE Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the state engineers society. It runs monthly talks, site tours and continuing education courses, plus youth STEM and MathCounts programs.
records.what_you_do: Attend a monthly talk or tour, take a continuing education course, or view the free presentation recordings.

schedule.text: Monthly chapter talks, plus tours and continuing education courses across the chapter year. The page gives no fixed meeting day.

locations.label: Chapter mailing address (c/o Temple University Civil Engineering)

cost.text: Online continuing education courses cost $5 per professional development hour. Some recorded talks are free to watch. The page gives no fee for monthly talks.

first_step.how: Email the chapter's meeting reservation address to hold a seat at the next monthly talk, or watch a free recorded talk first.
first_step.basis: Courses are offered to non-members and recorded talks are free to watch, but the page does not say whether non-members can attend the monthly talks, so the rating stops short of 4.
first_step.what_to_expect: Monthly talks are presentations by working engineers on a single topic, and the October talk is listed for 7 to 8 pm. The chapter serves licensed professional engineers, so expect a room of engineers, and it also runs site tours and short courses. Online courses cost $5 per professional development hour, and some recorded talks are free to watch first, while the page gives no fee for monthly talks.
first_visit_tips: Email the reservation address before a talk to hold a seat.
Watch a free recorded talk first if you want to see the format.
Check the event list for the meeting place, since the page does not give one for the October talk.

records.notes: The chapter site is current and lists a 2026 to 2027 program. The October talk and an October tour share one date, with no location listed for either. The February banquet date differs between two places on the site, so it is left out. Membership dues and eligibility are not on the page, only an application link. The phone is a Google Voice line that takes messages. Two near-duplicate mailing address rows were merged into one. Named on the site, not checked: Future City Philadelphia.
